title: PXAPI contextual diagnosis v1
description: Output of the contextual synthesis model (Confluence 39846055 §9): evidence-bound claims that join website evidence, business context and targeted evidence into one diagnosis of the analysed website. Every claim names the evidence it rests on by identifier. A claim that is strategically relevant, and a claim that is a VERIFIED_FACT or a SUPPORTED_CONTEXTUAL_INFERENCE, references at least one website, business or market evidence item; a HYPOTHESIS may rest on nothing. A contradiction between sources is stated explicitly as an UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT claim carrying the conflicting references — never silently resolved. An empty claims array means no claim could be made and says nothing about the website.

run_id.description: Required. The Analysis Run this diagnosis belongs to.

generated_at.description: Required. When the diagnosis was generated.

producer_ref.description: Required. What produced the diagnosis; synthesis models are interchangeable behind this shape.

website_evidence_refs.description: Required. The website-evidence artifacts the diagnosis was synthesised from (the baseline pass and, when it ran, the targeted pass). At least one; an empty array is rejected, because a diagnosis without website evidence is not a diagnosis of the website.

business_context_ref.description: Required. The business-context artifact the diagnosis was synthesised from.

business_intent_set_ref.description: Required. The business-intent-set artifact that steered the targeted pass the diagnosis draws on.

market_evidence_refs.description: Required. The market-evidence artifacts the diagnosis was synthesised from. An empty array means no market evidence was used. Market evidence has no v1 contract; it is referenced by artifact identity and type only.

inputs.description: Required. The artifacts the diagnosis was synthesised from, by reference. The diagnosis never copies their content.

claims.description: Required. The evidence-bound claims of the diagnosis. An empty array means no claim could be made; it is never a finding about the website.

claim_id.description: Required. The stable identity of this claim; product-diagnosis recommendations reference it.

claim.description: Required. The claim itself, in evidence language: what the sources establish, infer or leave open about the website in its business context.

website_evidence_refs.description: Required. The evidence_ids of the website-evidence items the claim rests on. An empty array means the claim rests on no website evidence.

business_evidence_refs.description: Required. The fact_ids of the business-context facts the claim rests on. An empty array means the claim rests on no business fact.

market_evidence_refs.description: Required. The identifiers of the market-evidence items the claim rests on. An empty array means the claim rests on no market evidence.

claim_type.description: Required. The authority of the claim, ordered HYPOTHESIS < SUPPORTED_CONTEXTUAL_INFERENCE < VERIFIED_FACT; a VERIFIED_FACT or SUPPORTED_CONTEXTUAL_INFERENCE references at least one evidence item. UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT marks a claim whose sources contradict each other and which is left open with its conflict stated, never resolved by choosing a side.

strategic_relevance.description: Required. Whether the claim passed the entrepreneur question (Confluence 39846055 §3.5): would it matter to the owner's business decision? A relevant claim references at least one evidence item; false means the claim is recorded but carries no strategic weight.

confidence.description: Required. Confidence in the claim on the 0..5 scale.

description.description: Required. What the sources disagree about, in evidence language, without deciding which side is right.

conflicting_refs.description: Required. The identifiers (evidence_ids, fact_ids or market-evidence identifiers) whose statements contradict each other. At least two, because a conflict has two sides; an empty array is rejected.

conflict.description: Conditional. Present if and only if claim_type is UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT: what the sources disagree about and which references disagree. Forbidden for every other claim type, where no conflict exists.
